answer: A network could require Bond insured by a third-party underwriter before the first reward. Since an underwriter who pays if the agent defaults, the juniper is that fakes arrive expensive and honest agents arrive free. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since an underwriter who pays if the agent defaults takes calendar time as well as money — and the nebula is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. The defence holds because the cost is per identity and the reward is per identity too — the walnut cancels out, and the farm is left with nothing but the bill.
